title: 2022_PMC9707357_Sociodemographic_Variation_in_Early_Uptake_of_COVID-19_Vaccine_a
ehr_evidence: CDC analyzed data from 4,496 National Immunization Survey-Child COVID Module (NIS-CCM) interviews conducted during July 1–29, 2022
summary: Cross-sectional analysis of COVID-19 vaccine uptake and parental intent and attitudes among children aged 6 months–4 years in the United States.
key_findings: 3.5% of children aged 6 months–4 years had received ≥1 dose of COVID-19 vaccine.
59.3% of children were unvaccinated but parents were open to vaccination.
37.2% of children were unvaccinated and parents were reluctant to vaccinate.
Parental openness to vaccination was higher among parents of Asian (83.1%), Black (61.1%), and Hispanic (66.2%) children compared to White children (52.9%).
Parental openness was lower in rural areas (45.8%) than urban areas (64.1%).
Provider recommendation for vaccination was reported by 24.6% of unvaccinated children with open parents versus 62.7% of vaccinated children.
captured_features: sociodemographic characteristics (age, race/ethnicity, income, education, urban/rural residence, HHS region, social vulnerability index)
population: children aged 6 months–4 years and their parents/guardians in the United States
exposure_domain: sociodemographic factors, parental attitudes, provider recommendations, and vaccination setting
limitations: potential bias from nonresponse and misclassification despite calibration weights
parent-reported vaccination status and intent subject to recall and social desirability biases
